cases.name: root-only
cases.note: The least a certificate can be: one region over the whole program, pricing nothing. A region with no terms is a bound of zero rather than a missing bound.

cases.name: nested-and-touching
cases.note: A group holding two alternation branches that meet end to end, with a quantifier body inside the second of them.

cases.name: empty-region
cases.note: A group with nothing in it compiles to two saves and no body between them, so a region of zero width is a real thing rather than a mistake.

cases.name: no-regions
cases.note: A certificate with no root has nothing to be the pattern's bound.

cases.name: root-is-not-a-root
cases.note: Region 0 is the root by position, and has to say so as well.

cases.name: root-has-a-parent
cases.note: Nothing encloses the whole program.

cases.name: root-starts-late
cases.note: A root that misses the first instruction prices less than the pattern.

cases.name: root-stops-early
cases.note: And a root that stops short of the last one prices less as well.

cases.name: two-roots
cases.note: Only region 0 is the root, or the tree has two places to start from.

cases.name: parent-above-its-child
cases.note: A parent at or above its child's index is what a cycle looks like from here, and refusing it is what makes the tree a tree without a walk.

cases.name: range-runs-backwards
cases.note: A region that ends before it starts covers no instruction at all.

cases.name: child-outside-its-parent
cases.note: A child reaching past its parent would be priced by neither.

cases.name: child-starts-before-its-parent
cases.note: The other half of the nesting rule, and the reason it is a refusal of its own rather than the sibling one: reaching back before the parent begins is a tree that does not nest, not two children colliding.

cases.name: siblings-overlap
cases.note: Two children sharing an instruction would have it counted twice, or by whichever of them the composition rule reached first.

cases.name: siblings-out-of-order
cases.note: Disjoint but backwards is refused too: the compiler emits regions as it flattens the AST, so source order costs a correct analyzer nothing and lets the checker settle both halves of the sibling rule in one pass.

cases.name: siblings-meet
cases.note: Meeting end to end is not overlapping, which is the common case.

cases.name: sum-names-terms-that-are-not-there
cases.note: An empty term table prices nothing, whatever a region claims.

cases.name: sum-runs-past-the-table
cases.note: And a sum may not reach past the last term either. Asked for a bound anyway, the engine answers rather than reading past the end.

cases.name: term-worth-nothing
cases.note: A term with no coefficient contributes nothing, so it says nothing that an empty sum does not say more clearly — and it would make every rule below conditional on a coefficient.

cases.name: base-of-zero
cases.note: 0^n is 1 at n = 0 and 0 after that. No bound has that shape, and one that vanishes on longer subjects would look like a bound that holds.

cases.name: degree-past-the-cap
cases.note: A power the soundness argument has no rule for.

cases.name: linear-claim-with-a-growing-base
cases.note: Linear means c * (n + 1). An exponential term is not that.

cases.name: linear-claim-with-a-square
cases.note: Nor is a square, however modest its coefficient.

cases.name: linear-claim-that-holds
cases.note: The Pike bound of DESIGN.md section 5: a constant and a term in n.

cases.name: polynomial
cases.note: 3 + 2n + n^2, evaluated left to right in counter arithmetic.

cases.name: exponential
cases.note: 2^n is a number until it is not, which happens at n = 53.

cases.name: at-the-saturation-point
cases.note: Exactly 2^53 - 1 is a bound a caller can pass back as a cost limit.

cases.name: one-past-the-saturation-point
cases.note: One more is not, and comes back as a refusal rather than as the cap.

cases.name: product-that-would-saturate
cases.note: The pre-check is on the operands, so the product never happens.

cases.name: product-that-just-fits
cases.note: And the one below it is exact.

cases.name: at-the-stack-ceiling
cases.note: The largest stack bound a stack limit could name.

cases.name: past-the-stack-ceiling
cases.note: One entry more, which no limit could accept, so it is not a number.

cases.name: at-the-memory-ceiling
cases.note: The section 3 byte ceiling, which is the largest reservation there is.

cases.name: past-the-memory-ceiling
cases.note: One byte more is refused as memory and still fine as cost, which is the whole difference between the three projections.

cases.name: children-are-not-summed-behind-the-accessor
cases.note: The pattern's bound is the root's bound. Nothing adds the children in, because the composition rule that would justify it does not exist yet.

note: Generated by pcretruste.engine.certificate_corpus. Each case hands the engine's bound-certificate checker one certificate and asks for the three bounds it prices, at every subject length below. Every implementation of the engine has to give exactly these answers: the same verdict, and the same number or the same refusal. A bound of null is the ExceedsBudget of DESIGN.md section 2.4, which is a refusal rather than a number and never a saturated counter.
